claims: Jehovah's Witnesses are a millennialist, restorationist Christian denomination.
Jehovah's Witnesses practice door-to-door evangelism.
Jehovah's Witnesses use the New World Translation Bible.
Jehovah's Witnesses refuse blood transfusions.
Jehovah's Witnesses refuse military service.
Jehovah's Witnesses refuse holiday celebrations.
Jehovah's Witnesses were founded by Charles Taze Russell in the 1870s.
Jehovah's Witnesses believe in an imminent Armageddon.
Jehovah's Witnesses believe that only 144,000 people go to heaven.
Jehovah's Witnesses believe others live on a paradise Earth.
Jehovah's Witnesses believe in one almighty God, Jehovah.
Jehovah's Witnesses reject the Trinity.
Jehovah's Witnesses consider the Trinity unscriptural.
Jehovah's Witnesses view Jesus as God's first creation.
Jehovah's Witnesses often identify Jesus as Michael the Archangel.
Jehovah's Witnesses view Jesus as the Son of God.
Jehovah's Witnesses do not view Jesus as equal to God.
Jehovah's Witnesses do not believe in hellfire.
Jehovah's Witnesses do not believe in an immortal soul.
Jehovah's Witnesses believe the dead cease to exist.
Jehovah's Witnesses believe in resurrection.
Jehovah's Witnesses believe God's Kingdom is a literal government in heaven.
Jehovah's Witnesses believe Jesus has been ruling since 1914.
Jehovah's Witnesses consider Jehovah the only proper name for God.
Jehovah's Witnesses conduct active, organized door-to-door witnessing.
Jehovah's Witnesses conduct public witnessing.
Jehovah's Witnesses conduct telephone witnessing.
Jehovah's Witnesses remain politically neutral.
Jehovah's Witnesses refuse to vote.
Jehovah's Witnesses refuse to run for office.
Jehovah's Witnesses do not celebrate birthdays.
Jehovah's Witnesses do not celebrate Christmas.
Jehovah's Witnesses do not celebrate Easter.
Jehovah's Witnesses do not celebrate holidays deemed to have pagan origins.
Jehovah's Witnesses prohibit premarital sex.
Jehovah's Witnesses prohibit homosexuality.
Jehovah's Witnesses prohibit intoxication.
Jehovah's Witnesses practice shunning (disfellowshipping).
Jehovah's Witnesses break all social contact with members who violate rules or choose to leave.
Jehovah's Witnesses have a central Governing Body in Warwick, NY.
The Governing Body sets doctrine and direction.
Jehovah's Witnesses fund their work by voluntary donations.
Jehovah's Witnesses do not tithe.
Jehovah's Witnesses do not pay clergy.
Jehovah's Witnesses hold meetings in Kingdom Halls.
Information and Bible study materials are available on jw.org.
Charles Taze Russell founded the Bible Student movement in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, in the 1870s.
Jehovah's Witnesses adopted the name Jehovah's Witnesses in 1931.
Jehovah's Witnesses adopted the name Jehovah's Witnesses to distinguish themselves from other Bible student groups.
